newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen to hold parliamentary vote on time.
newsitem.headline: Yemen to hold parliamentary vote on time.

text.p: Yemen plans to hold next year's parliamentary elections on time despite threats by opposition parties to boycott the polls, the first since the country's 1994 civil war, an official source said on Friday.
"The elections will take place on April 27 as set before and will not be postponed," he told Reuters. "We will not allow a constitutional vacuum, even if some parties boycott the elections."

The Islamist Islah Party, major partner in the ruling coalition, and six other opposition parties hinted at a joint news conference on Thursday they might boycott the vote and insisted on guarantees for free and fair elections.
They demanded reform of a committee in charge of the ballot and a review of voter lists after alleging the body committed violations during voter registration, which ended on August 31.
"The final word on these allegations or on any other violations, if found, is the duty of court," the source added.
President Ali Abdullah Saleh said last month his country planned to invite international observers to monitor the ballot to ensure its fairness.

International observers monitored the last poll in 1993 when 22 parties vied for 301 seats in parliament. Saleh's General People's Congress won a majority, followed by Islah and the opposition Yemen Socialist Party (YSP).
The three parties governed Yemen until the YSP, some of whose leaders launched the civil war separatist campaign, was dismissed from the coalition.
An opposition source told Reuters on Friday that leaders of opposition parties met Saleh on Thursday to press their election demands.

"But the meeting failed to reach any solutions," he said. "We will not give up on our demands and we will continue our dialogue with the president before issuing our final position on our participation in the elections."
